items.heading: Most "Is Nursing a Good
items.text: Most "is nursing a good career" articles only talk about a BSc Nursing graduate's path. That skips the first real decision most Indian nursing aspirants actually face: which of the three legal entry routes to take, and why that choice shapes your ceiling for a decade or more.

rows: 10th or 12th pass depending on the state (most states now require 12th)

Rural PHCs, sub-centres, community and maternal-child health work, not general hospital ward duty Capped early. Moving into hospital staff-nurse roles or abroad routes needs a bridge into GNM or Post Basic BSc later, not a direct jump.
12th pass, any stream (Science is common but not always mandatory), usual minimum age around 17

Hospital staff nurse from day one, similar day-to-day clinical scope to a fresh BSc graduate in most wards Real ceiling sits below a BSc for M.Sc admission, teaching roles, and some international licensing routes unless you complete a Post Basic BSc Nursing bridge afterward.
12th with Physics, Chemistry, Biology (PCB); many states and institutes now require a qualifying NEET score

Hospital staff nurse, same entry point as GNM, but the degree is the direct step into M.Sc Nursing, faculty roles, and most international licensing processes Highest ceiling of the three routes, the only one that opens M.Sc Nursing, nurse-educator work, and the fastest paperwork route for several abroad licensing pathways without an extra bridge course.

figures.source: Fresh BSc-qualified nurses in several private-sector roles report starting pay in the ₹12,000-18,000/month range, below the entry-level minimum wage benchmark in a number of other industries, according to public health workforce analysis.
